messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Research the Market** | • Look up recent sales of the same make/model on sites like Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, and Facebook Marketplace.
• Check local classifieds and music‑store listings. | Knowing the going rate helps you price competitively and avoid over‑ or under‑pricing. | | **2. Clean & Maintain** | • Give the guitar a thorough wipe‑down (use a microfiber cloth, a mild guitar cleaner, and a soft brush for the fretboard).
• Replace strings if they’re old or worn.
• Check for loose screws, cracks, or other damage. | A well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and can fetch a higher price. | | **3. Take High‑Quality Photos** | • Shoot in natural light; avoid harsh shadows.
• Capture the body, headstock, neck, fretboard, bridge, and any unique features.
• Include a close‑up of the serial number and any imperfections. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of returns or disputes. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | • Title: “Acoustic Guitar – [Brand] [Model] – Excellent Condition”
• Description: Include brand, model, year, condition, any upgrades, and why you’re selling.
• Mention any accessories (case, strap, picks). | Transparency builds trust and speeds up the sale. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform** | • **Online marketplaces**: Reverb (great for gear), eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace.
• **Local options**: Music‑store consignment, local classifieds, community bulletin boards.
• **Specialty forums**: Gearslutz, The Gear Page, or Reddit’s r/Guitar. | Different platforms reach different audiences; use a mix for maximum exposure. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | • Start slightly above your target price to allow room for negotiation.
• Consider adding a “+” sign (e.g., $350+) to signal flexibility. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a flexible price can close the deal faster. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Local pickup**: Safer, no shipping costs, instant payment.
• **Shipping**: Use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and a reputable carrier (UPS, FedEx, USPS). Get insurance and tracking. | Shipping expands your buyer pool but adds cost and risk; weigh the pros/cons. | | **8. Handle Payment Safely** | • For local sales: cash or Venmo/PayPal (with buyer protection).
• For online sales: PayPal Goods & Services, or a platform‑provided escrow. | Protect yourself from fraud and ensure you receive payment before handing over the guitar. | | **9. Meet Safely (if local)** | • Choose a public place (coffee shop, library, police station).
• Bring a friend or family member if possible.
• Verify the buyer’s ID if you’re handing over a large sum of cash. | Safety first—never meet in a secluded area or let a stranger into your home. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | • Sign a simple bill of sale (include serial number, condition, price, date, and both parties’ signatures).
• Keep a copy for your records. | A bill of sale protects both parties and can be useful for tax purposes. | | **11. Post‑Sale Follow‑Up** | • Thank the buyer and ask for a quick review if you used a marketplace.
• Offer to answer any post‑purchase questions. | Good customer service can lead to referrals and repeat business. | ### Quick Tips | Tip | How to Apply | |-----|--------------| | **Bundle Accessories** | Add a case, strap, or extra strings to sweeten the deal. | | **Offer a Demo** | If you’re comfortable, let the buyer try it out before buying. | | **Use a Consignment Shop** | If you’re short on time, let a local music store handle the sale for a commission. | | **Check for Trade‑Ins** | Some stores will buy or trade your guitar for a new one. | | **Tax Considerations** | Keep receipts and records; if you’re a hobbyist, you likely won’t owe taxes on a single sale. | ### Sample Listing (for Reverb) ``` Title: 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand: Yamaha - Model: FG800 - Year: 2015 - Condition: Light wear, no cracks, new strings installed - Features: Solid spruce top, nato/okume back & sides, 25.5" scale - Accessories: Original case, strap, picks - Reason for selling: Upgrading to a 12‑string Price: $350+ (Negotiable) Photos: [Attach 8–10 high‑resolution images] Contact: [Your email] / [Phone number] ``` Feel free to adapt this template to your own guitar’s specifics. Good luck with your sale!
